summary: The article examines how local education systems have approached technology integration and digital literacy since September 2023. It covers curriculum upgrades, efforts to close the digital divide, teacher training, assessment of impact, and community involvement. Quotes from officials, educators, and an expert illustrate a shift toward students being active creators rather than passive consumers of technology.
one_line: Local school boards and cities are embedding digital literacy in curriculums, closing the digital divide, training teachers, and measuring results after September 2023.
key_facts: Digital literacy has moved from a desirable skill to an essential aspect of education over the last decade, according to the article.
Dr. Angela Richardson, Chair of the Burgetown District School Board, said the goal is nurturing critical thinkers who can discern reliable from unreliable sources.
On November 15, 2023, the Winterville Education Council announced a sweeping digital literacy curriculum upgrade.
The Winterville Education Council upgrade includes coding classes beginning in the fourth grade and digital safety and ethics components in middle school curriculums.
Mrs. Carol Brady, a 6th-grade teacher at Franklin Elementary, uses interactive eBooks and online discussion platforms to promote student engagement.
On December 6, 2023, Mayor Tom Schneider of New Parkland unveiled a city-funded program offering subsidized internet access and affordable computers for low-income households.
School districts are partnering with tech companies to provide discounted devices and software for educational use.
The Eastwood Professional Development Center opened on September 9, 2023, offering workshops and online courses for teachers and administrators.
School districts are implementing assessment strategies that measure both quantitative aspects (devices used, hours of digital literacy instruction) and qualitative impact on learning and engagement.
Dr. Jason Willow, a leading authority on digital literacy, described improvements in students' research skills and online collaboration at an educator's conference.
Policies are being continually revised to be flexible, with distance learning during the Covid-19 pandemic cited as an example of unexpected challenges.
Local businesses, libraries, and neighborhood centers offer workshops and resources that complement school learning.
